title: Nimble model chooser + request builder visuals for Hosted API onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design a compact, developer-focused set of onboarding visuals that demonstrate the Hosted API flow: model selection chooser, inline request builder (text + structured params), and short multi-language code snippets. Deliver static screenshots for docs, annotated overlays for PR reviewers, and exportable assets for the docs team. Aim for minimal visual noise, clear affordances for model variants, and copy that orients first-time users to the trade-offs between latency/cost/quality.
acceptance_criteria: Three desktop screenshots: model chooser (default state), request builder filled sample, and combined request+response with streaming hint
Two mobile-width responsive screenshots (stacked flow) exported at 2x for docs and 3x for social assets
Code snippet set: JS (fetch), Python (requests), and curl — each matching the request builder payload shown in screenshots
Assets exported PNG and SVG where appropriate, named using the design asset naming convention: nimble-chooser-desktop@1x.png, nimble-request-builder-mobile@2x.png, nimble-snippets-js.svg, etc.
Figma file contains an annotated layer group 'DOCS_EXPORT_v1' with comments resolved and a final handoff page
Contrast and accessibility checks documented: all interactive elements meet AA text contrast and keyboard focus states are shown in overlay
comments: 2026-03-02 - Asha: Initial exploration completed. Two visual directions created: 'strip' (minimal horizontal selector) and 'card' (richer metadata per model). Leaning toward 'strip' for docs due to scanability.
2026-03-04 - Liam: Pulled strip direction into a prototype; added highlight for 'default recommended' model and cost/latency badge. Need copy tweak to make badges non-technical for first-run users.

2026-03-10 - Engineering (Marco): Confirmed API payload shape for code snippets; request builder form fields now match: model, prompt, max_tokens, temperature, streaming boolean.

design_decisions: Chosen 'strip' model chooser to reduce cognitive load and fit the tight docs column width
Limited visible model options to 4 in the primary chooser with 'Show more' to reduce initial complexity
Prioritized JS and Python snippets for the top fold; curl included for quick CLI verification. Omitted Ruby and Go for this release to keep the asset set small
Compact request builder shows 'advanced' toggle which expands optional params to keep the first-run UX simple
Used token-cost and latency badges with microcopy that explains trade-offs in plain language (not raw ms or token rates)
assets_to_deliver: nimble-snippets-js.svg - vector snippet for docs header
nimble-snippets-python.svg - vector snippet for docs header
QA_checks: Verify exported PNGs match Figma 'DOCS_EXPORT_v1' page and resolutions are correct
Check that code snippets copy-paste without extra invisible characters
Confirm the request payload shown in screenshots matches the example in the docs PR (github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842)
Run accessibility color-contrast test on all call-to-action labels
Confirm mobile screenshots render correctly in the docs CMS preview (mobile breakpoints)
notes: Avoid using internal model codenames in public screenshots; use user-friendly labels like 'balanced-l1' -> 'Balanced (low latency)'.
If streaming UI hint cannot be implemented visually by release date, include a small annotation callout in the screenshot copy instead.
Docs team requested a secondary set of black-on-white screenshots for the dark inline docs theme; created a separate Figma page 'DOCS_EXPORT_dark' as a fallback.
